newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks edge up slightly by lunch break.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks edge up slightly by lunch break.

text.p: Thai stocks advanced slightly in thin trade by the lunch break on Friday as investors, especially foreigners, stayed on the sidelines waiting for an economic rehabilitation plan from the government, brokers said.
"There's no positive news to boost investment. Most investors are waiting for the government's economic rehabilitation plan," said Bunsom Kesapradist of Asia Credit.
The composite SET index rose 1.86 points to 635.86 on 1.9 billion baht turnover by the lunch break.
Thai Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya said on Thursday the government will unveil a comprehensive economic plan within two weeks.
Brokers said the ongoing weakness of the baht was a negative factor preventing investors from entering the market.
The baht was quoted around 32.05/32.10 per dollar in onshore markets by lunch on Friday. It fell to a record low level of 32.70 baht per dollar early on Thursday.
Most of the key sectors gained on the bourse by midday.
Nava Finance topped the active list, falling 0.75 baht to 26.00. -- Suthep Chawla (662) 252-9950
